log: Working out who would actually buy this
Rechecking product fit for the same audiences; market evidence is retained

Coverage gaps. (1) Buyer voices: direct Reddit, Indie Hackers and Hacker News threads did not surface through this search tool; most retrieved pages are review, comparison or alternatives sites with affiliate-shaped incentives, and several appear to restate each other — treat agreement between them as one source, not corroboration. Several of those pages (comparedge, reloop, sequenzy, dreamlit, encharge) sell or promote competing products, so their counterevidence on pricing and feature limits may be adversarial; it is reported because it is specific and checkable, not because it is disinterested. (2) An agency / implementation-partner channel candidate was attempted and dropped: Framer and Webflow searches returned only template and SEO marketing, and no public source states whether Loops supports multiple client workspaces or sub-accounts, so there was no evidence of a buying situation. (3) No independent inbox-placement or deliverability study for Loops was found, and no SLA or uptime commitment appears anywhere in the supplied or searched material — this is the central unresolved objection for every candidate that would move production transactional mail. (4) Pricing between the $49 (5,000 contacts) and $399 (100,000 contacts) points is third-party-reported only and should be confirmed against loops.so/pricing. (5) Geography and language were unspecified and no boundary was imposed; all evidence found happens to be English-language, which is a sampling artefact of the search tool rather than a finding. (6) Instapaper and Slack appear in the supplied brief as email examples, not as confirmed Loops customers, and this search did not corroborate them as customers.
7 audience(s) mapped; 0 worth exploring first. Commercial priority is a hypothesis, not a response-rate forecast.
